Unlike traditional potato gnocchi that require boiling and mashing tubers, these light Italian dumplings rely on a creamy base of whole milk ricotta combined with finely chopped spinach and seasoned with fragrant nutmeg. The soft mixture comes together in minutes, requiring only a gentle folding of flour and parmesan cheese before being shaped into delicate spheres. Boiling them takes less than three minutes, making this an ideal meal for busy evenings when you want restaurant-quality comfort food without spending hours in the kitchen. A simple finishing drizzle of brown butter sauce and fresh sage leaves brings out the subtle richness of the dumplings, creating a beautifully balanced main dish that pairs wonderfully with a crisp green salad and chilled white wine.
